    18	import contextvars
    19	import os
    20	import signal
    21	import socket
    22	import subprocess

    26	from . import format_helpers

    28	
    29	class Handle:
    30	    """Object returned by callback registration methods."""
    31	
    32	    __slots__ = ('_callback', '_args', '_cancelled', '_loop',
    33	                 '_source_traceback', '_repr', '__weakref__',
    34	                 '_context')
    35	
    36	    def __init__(self, callback, args, loop, context=None):
    37	        if context is None:
    38	            context = contextvars.copy_context()
    39	        self._context = context
    40	        self._loop = loop
    41	        self._callback = callback
    42	        self._args = args
    43	        self._cancelled = False
    44	        self._repr = None
    45	        if self._loop.get_debug():
    46	            self._source_traceback = format_helpers.extract_stack(
    47	                sys._getframe(1))
    48	        else:
    49	            self._source_traceback = None
    50	
    51	    def _repr_info(self):
    52	        info = [self.__class__.__name__]
    53	        if self._cancelled:
    54	            info.append('cancelled')
    55	        if self._callback is not None:
    56	            info.append(format_helpers._format_callback_source(
    57	                self._callback, self._args))
    58	        if self._source_traceback:
    59	            frame = self._source_traceback[-1]
    60	            info.append(f'created at {frame[0]}:{frame[1]}')
    61	        return info
    62	
    63	    def __repr__(self):
    64	        if self._repr is not None:
    65	            return self._repr
    66	        info = self._repr_info()
    67	        return '<{}>'.format(' '.join(info))
    68	
    69	    def get_context(self):
    70	        return self._context
    71	
    72	    def cancel(self):
    73	        if not self._cancelled:
    74	            self._cancelled = True
    75	            if self._loop.get_debug():
    76	                # Keep a representation in debug mode to keep callback and
    77	                # parameters. For example, to log the warning
    78	                # "Executing <Handle...> took 2.5 second"
    79	                self._repr = repr(self)
    80	            self._callback = None
    81	            self._args = None
    82	
    83	    def cancelled(self):
    84	        return self._cancelled
    85	
    86	    def _run(self):
    87	        try:
    88	            self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
    89	        except (SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt):
    90	            raise
    91	        except BaseException as exc:
    92	            cb = format_helpers._format_callback_source(
    93	                self._callback, self._args)
    94	            msg = f'Exception in callback {cb}'
    95	            context = {
    96	                'message': msg,
    97	                'exception': exc,
    98	                'handle': self,
    99	            }
   100	            if self._source_traceback:
   101	                context['source_traceback'] = self._source_traceback
   102	            self._loop.call_exception_handler(context)
   103	        self = None  # Needed to break cycles when an exception occurs.
   104	
   105	
   106	class TimerHandle(Handle):
   107	    """Object returned by timed callback registration methods."""
   108	
   109	    __slots__ = ['_scheduled', '_when']
   110	
   111	    def __init__(self, when, callback, args, loop, context=None):
   112	        super().__init__(callback, args, loop, context)
   113	        if self._source_traceback:
   114	            del self._source_traceback[-1]
   115	        self._when = when
   116	        self._scheduled = False
   117	
   118	    def _repr_info(self):
   119	        info = super()._repr_info()
   120	        pos = 2 if self._cancelled else 1
   121	        info.insert(pos, f'when={self._when}')
   122	        return info
   123	
   124	    def __hash__(self):
   125	        return hash(self._when)
   126	
   127	    def __lt__(self, other):
   128	        if isinstance(other, TimerHandle):
   129	            return self._when < other._when
   130	        return NotImplemented
   131	
   132	    def __le__(self, other):
   133	        if isinstance(other, TimerHandle):
   134	            return self._when < other._when or self.__eq__(other)
   135	        return NotImplemented
   136	
   137	    def __gt__(self, other):
   138	        if isinstance(other, TimerHandle):
   139	            return self._when > other._when
   140	        return NotImplemented
   141	
   142	    def __ge__(self, other):
   143	        if isinstance(other, TimerHandle):
   144	            return self._when > other._when or self.__eq__(other)
   145	        return NotImplemented
   146	
   147	    def __eq__(self, other):
   148	        if isinstance(other, TimerHandle):
   149	            return (self._when == other._when and
   150	                    self._callback == other._callback and
   151	                    self._args == other._args and
   152	                    self._cancelled == other._cancelled)
   153	        return NotImplemented
   154	
   155	    def cancel(self):
   156	        if not self._cancelled:
   157	            self._loop._timer_handle_cancelled(self)
   158	        super().cancel()
   159	
   160	    def when(self):
   161	        """Return a scheduled callback time.
   162	
   163	        The time is an absolute timestamp, using the same time
   164	        reference as loop.time().
   165	        """
   166	        return self._when
   167	
   168	
   169	class AbstractServer:
   170	    """Abstract server returned by create_server()."""
   171	
   172	    def close(self):
   173	        """Stop serving.  This leaves existing connections open."""
   174	        raise NotImplementedError
   175	
   176	    def get_loop(self):
   177	        """Get the event loop the Server object is attached to."""
   178	        raise NotImplementedError
   179	
   180	    def is_serving(self):
   181	        """Return True if the server is accepting connections."""
   182	        raise NotImplementedError
   183	
   184	    async def start_serving(self):
   185	        """Start accepting connections.
   186	
   187	        This method is idempotent, so it can be called when
   188	        the server is already being serving.
   189	        """
   190	        raise NotImplementedError
   191	
   192	    async def serve_forever(self):
   193	        """Start accepting connections until the coroutine is cancelled.
   194	
   195	        The server is closed when the coroutine is cancelled.
   196	        """
   197	        raise NotImplementedError
   198	
   199	    async def wait_closed(self):
   200	        """Coroutine to wait until service is closed."""
   201	        raise NotImplementedError
   202	
   203	    async def __aenter__(self):
   204	        return self
   205	
   206	    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
   207	        self.close()
   208	        await self.wait_closed()
   209	
   210	
   211	class AbstractEventLoop:
   212	    """Abstract event loop."""
   213	
   214	    # Running and stopping the event loop.
   215	
   216	    def run_forever(self):
   217	        """Run the event loop until stop() is called."""
   218	        raise NotImplementedError
   219	
   220	    def run_until_complete(self, future):
   221	        """Run the event loop until a Future is done.
   222	
   223	        Return the Future's result, or raise its exception.
   224	        """
   225	        raise NotImplementedError
   226	
   227	    def stop(self):
   228	        """Stop the event loop as soon as reasonable.
   229	
   230	        Exactly how soon that is may depend on the implementation, but
   231	        no more I/O callbacks should be scheduled.
   232	        """
   233	        raise NotImplementedError
   234	
   235	    def is_running(self):
   236	        """Return whether the event loop is currently running."""
   237	        raise NotImplementedError
   238	
   239	    def is_closed(self):
   240	        """Returns True if the event loop was closed."""
   241	        raise NotImplementedError
   242	
   243	    def close(self):
   244	        """Close the loop.
   245	
   246	        The loop should not be running.
   247	
   248	        This is idempotent and irreversible.
   249	
   250	        No other methods should be called after this one.
   251	        """
   252	        raise NotImplementedError
   253	
   254	    async def shutdown_asyncgens(self):
   255	        """Shutdown all active asynchronous generators."""
   256	        raise NotImplementedError
   257	
   258	    async def shutdown_default_executor(self):
   259	        """Schedule the shutdown of the default executor."""
   260	        raise NotImplementedError
   261	
   262	    # Methods scheduling callbacks.  All these return Handles.
   263	
   264	    def _timer_handle_cancelled(self, handle):
   265	        """Notification that a TimerHandle has been cancelled."""
   266	        raise NotImplementedError
   267	
   268	    def call_soon(self, callback, *args, context=None):
   269	        return self.call_later(0, callback, *args, context=context)
   270	
   271	    def call_later(self, delay, callback, *args, context=None):
   272	        raise NotImplementedError
   273	
   274	    def call_at(self, when, callback, *args, context=None):
   275	        raise NotImplementedError
   276	
   277	    def time(self):
   278	        raise NotImplementedError
   279	
   280	    def create_future(self):
   281	        raise NotImplementedError
   282	
   283	    # Method scheduling a coroutine object: create a task.
   284	
   285	    def create_task(self, coro, *, name=None, context=None):
   286	        raise NotImplementedError
   287	
   288	    # Methods for interacting with threads.
   289	
   290	    def call_soon_threadsafe(self, callback, *args, context=None):
   291	        raise NotImplementedError
   292	
   293	    def run_in_executor(self, executor, func, *args):
   294	        raise NotImplementedError
   295	
   296	    def set_default_executor(self, executor):
   297	        raise NotImplementedError
   298	
   299	    # Network I/O methods returning Futures.
   300	
   301	    async def getaddrinfo(self, host, port, *,
   302	                          family=0, type=0, proto=0, flags=0):
   303	        raise NotImplementedError
   304	
   305	    async def getnameinfo(self, sockaddr, flags=0):
   306	        raise NotImplementedError
   307	
   308	    async def create_connection(
   309	            self, protocol_factory, host=None, port=None,
   310	            *, ssl=None, family=0, proto=0,
   311	            flags=0, sock=None, local_addr=None,
   312	            server_hostname=None,
   313	            ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   314	            ssl_shutdown_timeout=None,
   315	            happy_eyeballs_delay=None, interleave=None):
   316	        raise NotImplementedError
   317	
   318	    async def create_server(
   319	            self, protocol_factory, host=None, port=None,
   320	            *, family=socket.AF_UNSPEC,
   321	            flags=socket.AI_PASSIVE, sock=None, backlog=100,
   322	            ssl=None, reuse_address=None, reuse_port=None,
   323	            ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   324	            ssl_shutdown_timeout=None,
   325	            start_serving=True):
   326	        """A coroutine which creates a TCP server bound to host and port.
   327	
   328	        The return value is a Server object which can be used to stop
   329	        the service.
   330	
   331	        If host is an empty string or None all interfaces are assumed
   332	        and a list of multiple sockets will be returned (most likely
   333	        one for IPv4 and another one for IPv6). The host parameter can also be
   334	        a sequence (e.g. list) of hosts to bind to.
   335	
   336	        family can be set to either AF_INET or AF_INET6 to force the
   337	        socket to use IPv4 or IPv6. If not set it will be determined
   338	        from host (defaults to AF_UNSPEC).
   339	
   340	        flags is a bitmask for getaddrinfo().
   341	
   342	        sock can optionally be specified in order to use a preexisting
   343	        socket object.
   344	
   345	        backlog is the maximum number of queued connections passed to
   346	        listen() (defaults to 100).
   347	
   348	        ssl can be set to an SSLContext to enable SSL over the
   349	        accepted connections.
   350	
   351	        reuse_address tells the kernel to reuse a local socket in
   352	        TIME_WAIT state, without waiting for its natural timeout to
   353	        expire. If not specified will automatically be set to True on
   354	        UNIX.
   355	
   356	        reuse_port tells the kernel to allow this endpoint to be bound to
   357	        the same port as other existing endpoints are bound to, so long as
   358	        they all set this flag when being created. This option is not
   359	        supported on Windows.
   360	
   361	        ssl_handshake_timeout is the time in seconds that an SSL server
   362	        will wait for completion of the SSL handshake before aborting the
   363	        connection. Default is 60s.
   364	
   365	        ssl_shutdown_timeout is the time in seconds that an SSL server
   366	        will wait for completion of the SSL shutdown procedure
   367	        before aborting the connection. Default is 30s.
   368	
   369	        start_serving set to True (default) causes the created server
   370	        to start accepting connections immediately.  When set to False,
   371	        the user should await Server.start_serving() or Server.serve_forever()
   372	        to make the server to start accepting connections.
   373	        """
   374	        raise NotImplementedError
   375	
   376	    async def sendfile(self, transport, file, offset=0, count=None,
   377	                       *, fallback=True):
   378	        """Send a file through a transport.
   379	
   380	        Return an amount of sent bytes.
   381	        """
   382	        raise NotImplementedError
   383	
   384	    async def start_tls(self, transport, protocol, sslcontext, *,
   385	                        server_side=False,
   386	                        server_hostname=None,
   387	                        ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   388	                        ssl_shutdown_timeout=None):
   389	        """Upgrade a transport to TLS.
   390	
   391	        Return a new transport that *protocol* should start using
   392	        immediately.
   393	        """
   394	        raise NotImplementedError
   395	
   396	    async def create_unix_connection(
   397	            self, protocol_factory, path=None, *,
   398	            ssl=None, sock=None,
   399	            server_hostname=None,
   400	            ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   401	            ssl_shutdown_timeout=None):
   402	        raise NotImplementedError
   403	
   404	    async def create_unix_server(
   405	            self, protocol_factory, path=None, *,
   406	            sock=None, backlog=100, ssl=None,
   407	            ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   408	            ssl_shutdown_timeout=None,
   409	            start_serving=True):
   410	        """A coroutine which creates a UNIX Domain Socket server.
   411	
   412	        The return value is a Server object, which can be used to stop
   413	        the service.
   414	
   415	        path is a str, representing a file system path to bind the
   416	        server socket to.
   417	
   418	        sock can optionally be specified in order to use a preexisting
   419	        socket object.
   420	
   421	        backlog is the maximum number of queued connections passed to
   422	        listen() (defaults to 100).
   423	
   424	        ssl can be set to an SSLContext to enable SSL over the
   425	        accepted connections.
   426	
   427	        ssl_handshake_timeout is the time in seconds that an SSL server
   428	        will wait for the SSL handshake to complete (defaults to 60s).
   429	
   430	        ssl_shutdown_timeout is the time in seconds that an SSL server
   431	        will wait for the SSL shutdown to finish (defaults to 30s).
   432	
   433	        start_serving set to True (default) causes the created server
   434	        to start accepting connections immediately.  When set to False,
   435	        the user should await Server.start_serving() or Server.serve_forever()
   436	        to make the server to start accepting connections.
   437	        """
   438	        raise NotImplementedError
   439	
   440	    async def connect_accepted_socket(
   441	            self, protocol_factory, sock,
   442	            *, ssl=None,
   443	            ssl_handshake_timeout=None,
   444	            ssl_shutdown_timeout=None):
   445	        """Handle an accepted connection.
   446	
   447	        This is used by servers that accept connections outside of
   448	        asyncio, but use asyncio to handle connections.
   449	
   450	        This method is a coroutine.  When completed, the coroutine
   451	        returns a (transport, protocol) pair.
   452	        """
   453	        raise NotImplementedError
   454	
   455	    async def create_datagram_endpoint(self, protocol_factory,
   456	                                       local_addr=None, remote_addr=None, *,
   457	                                       family=0, proto=0, flags=0,
   458	                                       reuse_address=None, reuse_port=None,
   459	                                       allow_broadcast=None, sock=None):
   460	        """A coroutine which creates a datagram endpoint.
   461	
   462	        This method will try to establish the endpoint in the background.
   463	        When successful, the coroutine returns a (transport, protocol) pair.
   464	
   465	        protocol_factory must be a callable returning a protocol instance.
   466	
   467	        socket family AF_INET, socket.AF_INET6 or socket.AF_UNIX depending on
   468	        host (or family if specified), socket type SOCK_DGRAM.
   469	
   470	        reuse_address tells the kernel to reuse a local socket in
   471	        TIME_WAIT state, without waiting for its natural timeout to
   472	        expire. If not specified it will automatically be set to True on
   473	        UNIX.
   474	
   475	        reuse_port tells the kernel to allow this endpoint to be bound to
   476	        the same port as other existing endpoints are bound to, so long as
   477	        they all set this flag when being created. This option is not
   478	        supported on Windows and some UNIX's. If the
   479	        :py:data:`~socket.SO_REUSEPORT` constant is not defined then this
   480	        capability is unsupported.
   481	
   482	        allow_broadcast tells the kernel to allow this endpoint to send
   483	        messages to the broadcast address.
   484	
   485	        sock can optionally be specified in order to use a preexisting
   486	        socket object.
   487	        """
   488	        raise NotImplementedError
   489	
   490	    # Pipes and subprocesses.
   491	
   492	    async def connect_read_pipe(self, protocol_factory, pipe):
   493	        """Register read pipe in event loop. Set the pipe to non-blocking mode.
   494	
   495	        protocol_factory should instantiate object with Protocol interface.
   496	        pipe is a file-like object.
   497	        Return pair (transport, protocol), where transport supports the
   498	        ReadTransport interface."""
   499	        # The reason to accept file-like object instead of just file descriptor
   500	        # is: we need to own pipe and close it at transport finishing
   501	        # Can got complicated errors if pass f.fileno(),
   502	        # close fd in pipe transport then close f and vice versa.
   503	        raise NotImplementedError
   504	
   505	    async def connect_write_pipe(self, protocol_factory, pipe):
   506	        """Register write pipe in event loop.
   507	
   508	        protocol_factory should instantiate object with BaseProtocol interface.
   509	        Pipe is file-like object already switched to nonblocking.
   510	        Return pair (transport, protocol), where transport support
   511	        WriteTransport interface."""
   512	        # The reason to accept file-like object instead of just file descriptor
   513	        # is: we need to own pipe and close it at transport finishing
   514	        # Can got complicated errors if pass f.fileno(),
   515	        # close fd in pipe transport then close f and vice versa.
   516	        raise NotImplementedError
   517

   617	
   618	class AbstractEventLoopPolicy:
   619	    """Abstract policy for accessing the event loop."""
   620	
   621	    def get_event_loop(self):
   622	        """Get the event loop for the current context.
   623	
   624	        Returns an event loop object implementing the AbstractEventLoop interface,
   625	        or raises an exception in case no event loop has been set for the
   626	        current context and the current policy does not specify to create one.
   627	
   628	        It should never return None."""
   629	        raise NotImplementedError
   630	
   631	    def set_event_loop(self, loop):
   632	        """Set the event loop for the current context to loop."""
   633	        raise NotImplementedError
   634	
   635	    def new_event_loop(self):
   636	        """Create and return a new event loop object according to this
   637	        policy's rules. If there's need to set this loop as the event loop for
   638	        the current context, set_event_loop must be called explicitly."""
   639	        raise NotImplementedError
   640	
   641	    # Child processes handling (Unix only).
   642	
   643	    def get_child_watcher(self):
   644	        "Get the watcher for child processes."
   645	        raise NotImplementedError
   646	
   647	    def set_child_watcher(self, watcher):
   648	        """Set the watcher for child processes."""
   649	        raise NotImplementedError
   650	
   651	
   652	class BaseDefaultEventLoopPolicy(AbstractEventLoopPolicy):
   653	    """Default policy implementation for accessing the event loop.
   654	
   655	    In this policy, each thread has its own event loop.  However, we
   656	    only automatically create an event loop by default for the main
   657	    thread; other threads by default have no event loop.
   658	
   659	    Other policies may have different rules (e.g. a single global
   660	    event loop, or automatically creating an event loop per thread, or
   661	    using some other notion of context to which an event loop is
   662	    associated).
   663	    """
   664	
   665	    _loop_factory = None
   666	
   667	    class _Local(threading.local):
   668	        _loop = None
   669	        _set_called = False
   670	
   671	    def __init__(self):
   672	        self._local = self._Local()
   673	
   674	    def get_event_loop(self):
   675	        """Get the event loop for the current context.
   676	
   677	        Returns an instance of EventLoop or raises an exception.
   678	        """
   679	        if (self._local._loop is None and
   680	                not self._local._set_called and
   681	                threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()):
   682	            stacklevel = 2
   683	            try:
   684	                f = sys._getframe(1)
   685	            except AttributeError:
   686	                pass
   687	            else:
   688	                # Move up the call stack so that the warning is attached
   689	                # to the line outside asyncio itself.
   690	                while f:
   691	                    module = f.f_globals.get('__name__')
   692	                    if not (module == 'asyncio' or module.startswith('asyncio.')):
   693	                        break
   694	                    f = f.f_back
   695	                    stacklevel += 1
   696	            import warnings
   697	            warnings.warn('There is no current event loop',
   698	                          DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=stacklevel)
   699	            self.set_event_loop(self.new_event_loop())
   700	
   701	        if self._local._loop is None:
   702	            raise RuntimeError('There is no current event loop in thread %r.'
   703	                               % threading.current_thread().name)
   704	
   705	        return self._local._loop
   706	
   707	    def set_event_loop(self, loop):
   708	        """Set the event loop."""
   709	        self._local._set_called = True
   710	        if loop is not None and not isinstance(loop, AbstractEventLoop):
   711	            raise TypeError(f"loop must be an instance of AbstractEventLoop or None, not '{type(loop).__name__}'")
   712	        self._local._loop = loop
   713	
   714	    def new_event_loop(self):
   715	        """Create a new event loop.
   716	
   717	        You must call set_event_loop() to make this the current event
   718	        loop.
   719	        """
   720	        return self._loop_factory()
   721	
   722	
   723	# Event loop policy.  The policy itself is always global, even if the
   724	# policy's rules say that there is an event loop per thread (or other
   725	# notion of context).  The default policy is installed by the first
   726	# call to get_event_loop_policy().
   727	_event_loop_policy = None
   728	
   729	# Lock for protecting the on-the-fly creation of the event loop policy.
   730	_lock = threading.Lock()
   731	
   732	
   733	# A TLS for the running event loop, used by _get_running_loop.
   734	class _RunningLoop(threading.local):
   735	    loop_pid = (None, None)
   736	
   737	
   738	_running_loop = _RunningLoop()
   739	
   740	
   741	def get_running_loop():
   742	    """Return the running event loop.  Raise a RuntimeError if there is none.
   743	
   744	    This function is thread-specific.
   745	    """
   746	    # NOTE: this function is implemented in C (see _asynciomodule.c)
   747	    loop = _get_running_loop()
   748	    if loop is None:
   749	        raise RuntimeError('no running event loop')
   750	    return loop
   751	
   752	
   753	def _get_running_loop():
   754	    """Return the running event loop or None.
   755	
   756	    This is a low-level function intended to be used by event loops.
   757	    This function is thread-specific.
   758	    """
   759	    # NOTE: this function is implemented in C (see _asynciomodule.c)
   760	    running_loop, pid = _running_loop.loop_pid
   761	    if running_loop is not None and pid == os.getpid():
   762	        return running_loop
   763	
   764	
   765	def _set_running_loop(loop):
   766	    """Set the running event loop.
   767	
   768	    This is a low-level function intended to be used by event loops.
   769	    This function is thread-specific.
   770	    """
   771	    # NOTE: this function is implemented in C (see _asynciomodule.c)
   772	    _running_loop.loop_pid = (loop, os.getpid())
   773	
   774	
   775	def _init_event_loop_policy():
   776	    global _event_loop_policy
   777	    with _lock:
   778	        if _event_loop_policy is None:  # pragma: no branch
   779	            from . import DefaultEventLoopPolicy
   780	            _event_loop_policy = DefaultEventLoopPolicy()
   781	
   782	
   783	def get_event_loop_policy():
   784	    """Get the current event loop policy."""
   785	    if _event_loop_policy is None:
   786	        _init_event_loop_policy()
   787	    return _event_loop_policy
   788	
   789	
   790	def set_event_loop_policy(policy):
   791	    """Set the current event loop policy.
   792	
   793	    If policy is None, the default policy is restored."""
   794	    global _event_loop_policy
   795	    if policy is not None and not isinstance(policy, AbstractEventLoopPolicy):
   796	        raise TypeError(f"policy must be an instance of AbstractEventLoopPolicy or None, not '{type(policy).__name__}'")
   797	    _event_loop_policy = policy
   798	
   799	
   800	def get_event_loop():
   801	    """Return an asyncio event loop.
   802	
   803	    When called from a coroutine or a callback (e.g. scheduled with call_soon
   804	    or similar API), this function will always return the running event loop.
   805	
   806	    If there is no running event loop set, the function will return
   807	    the result of `get_event_loop_policy().get_event_loop()` call.
   808	    """
   809	    # NOTE: this function is implemented in C (see _asynciomodule.c)
   810	    current_loop = _get_running_loop()
   811	    if current_loop is not None:
   812	        return current_loop
   813	    return get_event_loop_policy().get_event_loop()
   814	
   815	
   816	def set_event_loop(loop):
   817	    """Equivalent to calling get_event_loop_policy().set_event_loop(loop)."""
   818	    get_event_loop_policy().set_event_loop(loop)
   819	
   820	
   821	def new_event_loop():
   822	    """Equivalent to calling get_event_loop_policy().new_event_loop()."""
   823	    return get_event_loop_policy().new_event_loop()
   824	
   825	
   826	def get_child_watcher():
   827	    """Equivalent to calling get_event_loop_policy().get_child_watcher()."""
   828	    return get_event_loop_policy().get_child_watcher()
   829	
   830	
   831	def set_child_watcher(watcher):
   832	    """Equivalent to calling
   833	    get_event_loop_policy().set_child_watcher(watcher)."""
   834	    return get_event_loop_policy().set_child_watcher(watcher)
   835	
   836	
   837	# Alias pure-Python implementations for testing purposes.
   838	_py__get_running_loop = _get_running_loop
   839	_py__set_running_loop = _set_running_loop
   840	_py_get_running_loop = get_running_loop
   841	_py_get_event_loop = get_event_loop
   842	
   843	
   844	try:
   845	    # get_event_loop() is one of the most frequently called
   846	    # functions in asyncio.  Pure Python implementation is
   847	    # about 4 times slower than C-accelerated.
   848	    from _asyncio import (_get_running_loop, _set_running_loop,
   849	                          get_running_loop, get_event_loop)
   850	except ImportError:
   851	    pass
   852	else:
   853	    # Alias C implementations for testing purposes.
   854	    _c__get_running_loop = _get_running_loop
   855	    _c__set_running_loop = _set_running_loop
   856	    _c_get_running_loop = get_running_loop
   857	    _c_get_event_loop = get_event_loop
   858	
   859	
   860	if hasattr(os, 'fork'):
   861	    def on_fork():
   862	        # Reset the loop and wakeupfd in the forked child process.
   863	        if _event_loop_policy is not None:
   864	            _event_loop_policy._local = BaseDefaultEventLoopPolicy._Local()
   865	        _set_running_loop(None)
   866	        signal.set_wakeup_fd(-1)
   867	
   868	    os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=on_fork)
